metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Arnold, PA | Get a Cash Offer
metaDescription: Arnold, PA mineral owners along the Allegheny: get a no-pressure cash offer on your Marcellus royalty interest, explained in plain terms.
heroLead: Arnold sits along the Allegheny River, a former mill town where a lot of families hold mineral interests in outlying tracts rather than the town itself.
intro: Arnold is a compact river city, and most mineral ownership tied to it actually sits in the surrounding Westmoreland County farmland rather than within the city limits itself. If you or your family hold an interest connected to this area, it's likely a legacy tract passed down from relatives who farmed outside town before the mill economy took hold, and the mineral rights stayed with the family even as the surface changed hands or the town grew up around it.
That kind of layered history is exactly what we specialize in untangling. We start with your actual documents, not assumptions.

sections.heading: Where the minerals actually sit
paragraphs: Because Arnold itself is densely built, drilling activity connected to Arnold-area mineral owners typically comes from units in the surrounding, less developed parts of Westmoreland County. Your royalty is tied to the specific unit your acreage participates in, not to the city of Arnold generally, so confirming the exact parcel and unit matters more here than the city name on your address.
This region falls within Westmoreland County's wet-gas Marcellus territory, with EQT and CNX among the more active operators holding leasehold nearby.

sections.heading: Old river-town family land
paragraphs: A lot of Arnold-connected mineral interests trace back through several generations of the same family, often with deeds that predate the shale boom by decades. We do the title tracing through the Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds so you're not left digging through old paperwork on your own.

sections.heading: Getting a real number, not a guess
paragraphs: Once we confirm your net mineral acreage and decimal interest, we review your recent royalty statements and build an offer around your actual production history, then explain exactly how we arrived at it.

faqs.question: I live in Arnold but my family's minerals are elsewhere in the county. Do you still help?
faqs.answer: Yes. We evaluate the interest based on where the mineral acreage actually sits, not where you currently live.

faqs.question: My deed is decades old and hard to read. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: Not usually. We're accustomed to working from older recorded deeds and can trace the chain of title through the county recorder's office.

faqs.question: How do you handle multiple heirs who all inherited a share?
faqs.answer: We can work with each heir individually or coordinate a single closing for all interested parties, whichever is simpler for your family.
